newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Blue chips weaker on Nigerian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips weaker on Nigerian bourse.

text.p: Nigerian blue chips closed weaker on Monday, reflecting a persistent bearish mood and a flow out of shares into the money market, dealers said.
The all-share index closed at 8585.63 from 8592.32 on Friday.
Dealers said prices continued to tumble as investors joined the rush to sell.
A misunderstanding of a new clearing system and rising interest rates causing funds to start flowing from stocks to the money markets are responsible for the trend, dealers said.
Blue chips in the oil marketing sector and leading conglomerates slumped alongside falling banks and brewers.
Total fell 40 kobo to 59.00 naira while Agip lost 10 kobo to 21.20 naira and African Petroleum closed 56.95 naira, down five kobo.
Healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham joined the losers, closing 15 kobo down at 6.50 naira.
Conglomerates UAC dropped 10 kobo to 16.90 naira while PZ Industries was down five kobo at 29.30 naira. Cadbury also went down five kobo to 36.85 naira.
Nestle, however, continued its rise, closing 35 kobo up at 44.25 naira following its impressive full year result announced last month.
Flour Mills ended 10 kobo up at 16.65 naira after topping last week's gainers' chart ahead of Nestle.
FSB International Bank also rose five kobo to 4.30 naira because of its own good result.
Wema Bank also added two kobo to 2.85 naira on bargain hunting, traders said.
The biggest faller among the top banks on Monday was UBA, down 10 kobo to 11.70 naira.
